topics.title: Areas of a Sector and Segment of a Circle

concepts.name: Sector of a Circle
concepts.description: A sector is the region enclosed by two radii and the corresponding arc of a circle. Its area depends on the central angle subtended by the arc.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify sectors and calculate their areas using the appropriate formula.

concepts.name: Area of a Sector
concepts.description: The area of a sector is proportional to its central angle and is calculated using the formula (θ/360°) × πr².
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compute the area of a sector for a given radius and central angle.

concepts.name: Arc Length
concepts.description: The length of an arc is the portion of the circle's circumference corresponding to a central angle and is calculated using (θ/360°) × 2πr.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the length of an arc using the radius and central angle.

concepts.name: Segment of a Circle
concepts.description: A segment is the region bounded by a chord and its corresponding arc. It differs from a sector because it is not enclosed by radii.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between a sector and a segment of a circle.

concepts.name: Area of a Segment
concepts.description: The area of a segment is obtained by subtracting the area of the corresponding triangle from the area of the sector.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the area of a segment using sector and triangle areas.

concepts.name: Minor and Major Segments
concepts.description: A chord divides a circle into a minor segment and a major segment. Their areas together equal the total area of the circle.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and determine the areas of minor and major segments.

topics.title: Applications of Areas Related to Circles

concepts.name: Composite Figures
concepts.description: Many practical problems involve figures composed of sectors, segments, and other geometric shapes. Solving such problems requires decomposing the figure into simpler parts.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the area of composite figures involving circles.

concepts.name: Real-Life Applications
concepts.description: Concepts of sectors and segments are used in designing roads, gardens, machinery, architecture, and engineering structures.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve practical problems involving areas related to circles.

concepts.name: Selection of Appropriate Formula
concepts.description: Choosing the correct formula depends on whether the required region is a sector, segment, or a combination of geometric figures.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to select and apply the appropriate area formula for various circle-related problems.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Areas Related to Circles
concepts.description: This chapter summarizes the calculation of arc lengths, sector areas, segment areas, and their applications in solving geometric and real-world problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate and apply formulas for sectors, segments, and arc lengths to solve mathematical and practical problems.
